{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=8
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=16
# NOTE: SLURM's '--mem=0' requests all available memory on the node. This is
# the equivalent behavior in Flux.
#FLUX --mem-per-node=0
#FLUX --gpus=8

# NOTE: Flux does not have a token for nodename in the output/error file paths.
# The SLURM %N token has been omitted.
#FLUX -o {name}-{id}.out
#FLUX -e {name}-{id}.err

source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh

# Use partition/queue name to load OS-specific modulespath to use to override
# login node environment. The SLURM variable $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION has been
# replaced with the Flux equivalent, $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE.
if [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i ubuntu) = *Ubuntu* ]]; then
    module use /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i rhel8) = *RHEL8* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i rhel9) = *RHEL9* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i sles15) = *SLES15* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i centos8) = *CentOS8* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i rocky9) = *Rocky9* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
fi


module purge
module load rocm-5.4.2/ucx-1.13.1/ompi/4.1.4

tmp=/tmp/$USER/tmp-$$
mkdir -p $tmp

singularity run /shared/apps/bin/namd3_3.0a9.sif cp -r /examples ./examples-$$

singularity run --bind ./examples-$$:/examples-$$ --pwd /examples-$$ /shared/apps/bin/namd3_3.0a9.sif /opt/namd/bin/namd3 jac/jac.namd +p1 +setcpuaffinity --CUDASOAintegrate on +devices 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7

singularity run --bind ./examples-$$:/examples-$$ --pwd /examples-$$ /shared/apps/bin/namd3_3.0a9.sif /opt/namd/bin/namd3 apoa1/apoa1.namd +p1 +setcpuaffinity --CUDASOAintegrate on +devices 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7

singularity run --bind ./examples-$$:/examples-$$ --pwd /examples-$$ /shared/apps/bin/namd3_3.0a9.sif /opt/namd/bin/namd3 f1atpase/f1atpase.namd +p1 +setcpuaffinity --CUDASOAintegrate on +devices 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 

singularity run --bind ./examples-$$:/examples-$$ --pwd /examples-$$ /shared/apps/bin/namd3_3.0a9.sif /opt/namd/bin/namd3 stmv/stmv.namd +p1 +setcpuaffinity --CUDASOAintegrate on +devices 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7

# The SLURM variables $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST and $SLURM_JOB_ID have been replaced
# with the Flux equivalents $FLUX_JOB_NODELIST and $FLUX_JOB_ID.
cp -r ./examples-$$   $PWD/gpu8-$$-$FLUX_JOB_NODELIST-$FLUX_JOB_ID

rm -rf examples-$$/
"
}

issues: The job requests 8 tasks (`--ntasks-per-node=8`) but executes a series of four `singularity run` commands serially. Since these commands are not launched with a parallel launcher like `flux run`, only one of the 8 allocated tasks will be used at any given time, leaving the other 7 tasks completely idle for the duration of the job. This represents a significant underutilization of allocated resources.

The application is launched with the argument `+devices 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7`, which hardcodes the GPU device IDs. This practice bypasses the scheduler's resource assignment mechanism. The application should instead rely on environment variables (e.g., `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`) that Flux sets to discover which specific GPUs have been allocated to the job. Hardcoding device IDs can lead to resource conflicts on shared nodes and makes the script less portable.

There is a logical mismatch between the resources requested and how they are used. The job requests 8 tasks and 8 GPUs, suggesting a one-task-per-GPU model. However, the application is run as a single process that attempts to use all 8 GPUs. A more appropriate and efficient resource request for this usage pattern would be `#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=1` and `#FLUX --gpus-per-task=8`.
